diet.note: Based on the PBDB ecology entry for the genus.

timeRange.note: PBDB occurrences: Santonian (Niobrara) to Early–Middle Campanian (Pierre Shale). Ages are ICS stage bounds (Santonian base 85.7 Ma, Campanian top 72.2 Ma), so the range is broader than the fossils themselves.

text.en: Pteranodon was a flying reptile called a pterosaur, neither a dinosaur nor a bird. It had no teeth, and museum models give it wings about 5.5 metres (18 feet) across. It was common in North America in the Late Cretaceous, and its fossils come from Kansas, South Dakota and Wyoming. It probably ate fish.

uncertain.note: Wingspan, the usual size measure for pterosaurs, is not modelled in the schema; no verified body length found.
Only stage-level ages available (PBDB); the end bound uses the top of the Campanian although records are labelled Early–Middle Campanian.
PBDB places Pteranodon in Pteranodontia without naming a family; no verified source for Pteranodontidae was opened.
